newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Stay out of Zaire, UN Council tells foreign troops.
newsitem.headline: Stay out of Zaire, UN Council tells foreign troops.

text.p: The U.N. Security Council expressed grave concern on Friday over the deteriorating situation in Central Africa and warned states to stay out of the civil war in Zaire.

In a statement read at a formal meeting by Council President Njuguna Mahugu of Kenya, the 15-member body called "for an end to the hostilities and the withdrawal of all external forces, including mercenaries."

"The Council calls upon all states in the region to refrain...from any act, including cross-border incursions, which would threaten the sovereignty and territorial integrity of any state," the council said.

Rebels battling the Zaire army since October have extended their campaign and territory they hold from the borders of Rwanda and Uganda to Zaire's mineral-rich Shaba Province. They are said to have backing from Rwanda while Zaire is said to have hired mercenaries.
The council also again called for an international conference on peace, security and development among states in what is known as the Great Lakes region of Africa.

In the main, the statement served to back the mission of Algerian diplomat Mohammed Sahnoun, who left New York on Thursday as the new Central African representative for the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity.

The council urged all parties in the region to cooperate fully with Sahnoun and said member states should provide him with logistical support. Germany so far has contributed towards leasing a plane and communications equipment for him.

His assignment focuses on a civil war led by ethnic Tutsis in eastern Zaire, ethnic war in Burundi and collective trauma in Rwanda after the 1994 genocide by Hutus of up to 800,000 minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
These conflicts have spawned millions of refugees and displaced people, an arms race and deep hostilities between regional leaders.

The council demanded that all combatants allow humanitarian agencies to help refugees and others in need. "It underlines the obligations of all concerned to respect the relevant provisions of international humanitarian law," it said.
